column1: # Pronunciation overrides applied to every book.
# Kokoro never sees your letters, only phonemes. A name or loanword outside
# its dictionary is guessed from English spelling rules, and the guess is
# sometimes wrong. This file is where you correct those guesses once, for
# every book you convert.
# FORMAT
#   word <TAB> IPA <TAB> intended sound
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored. The third column is a
# note to yourself in whatever spelling makes sense to you -- it is never
# read by the pipeline, and it is what keeps the file reviewable without
# having to parse IPA.
# Matching is case-insensitive and handles possessives, so one entry covers
# "Ramirez" and "Ramirez's". It does not match across hyphens or inside
# longer words.
# NOTATION
# Kokoro uses IPA with a few of its own vowel symbols:
#   A = "ay" as in day        I = "eye" as in time
#   O = "oh" as in go         W = "ow" as in now
#   Y = "oy" as in boy        T = flapped t, as in American "water"
# Put the stress mark ˈ immediately before the stressed syllable, and the
# secondary stress mark ˌ before a lesser one.
# ADDING ENTRIES
#   1. python pipeline/extract.py <slug>
#   2. python pipeline/probe_names.py <slug>
# probe_names.py lists every proper noun in the book with the phonemes it
# will be given, commonest first, skipping anything already covered here.
# Read it, and add a line for each one that is wrong.
# Put a name here if it is a real name with a fixed pronunciation, so the
# next book you convert inherits it. Put it in books/<slug>/lexicon.tsv
# instead if it is peculiar to one book -- an invented name, or a word that
# book says differently.
# EXAMPLE
# Suppose probe_names.py shows a surname coming out with the stress on the
# wrong syllable. Add:
#   Ramirez
# Then re-run probe_names.py to confirm it no longer appears.
